attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his own view. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The draft keeps all three firm assertions. Nothing in them is hedged. 'They' refers to organisations paying for AI. That scope is implicit but is not lost in the draft, which correctly treats the statement as an observation.

contract.note: Zitron named no standard for 'compelling'. Reading it as credible controlled measurement of faster work with acceptable quality is an ordinary reading. Treating the three assertions separately and requiring non-technical users for the software assertion is fair. A narrower organisation-wide reading of the productivity assertion could change the result.

evidence.note: Preregistered randomised experiment, public in 2023: ChatGPT cut task time and raised quality on professional writing tasks. This is credible controlled evidence that existed well before the post.

Peer-reviewed workplace study published in 2025: about 15% more issues resolved per hour among support agents, measured against a comparison. Contradicts the claim that no evidence of speedup existed.
Klarna's own filing reports headcount falling and attributes the cuts partly to AI. This is a company disclosure, not an independent finding, and it does not isolate positions that AI replaced.
METR randomised trial found a 19% slowdown among experienced developers. It does not cancel the positive studies and does not test non-technical users.
METR's follow-up shows weak signs of speedup but warns the data are unreliable because of selection effects. It concerns professional developers, not non-technical users.

reviews.rationale: The claim that there was no compelling evidence AI speeds people up is contradicted. Two credible controlled studies, public in 2023 and 2025, found faster work with maintained or better quality. The replacement assertion stays unsettled because Klarna's filing is only a company disclosure. The software-delivery assertion stays unsettled because no comparison of non-technical users is in the packet. Since none of the three parts is supported and one is contradicted, the outcome is contradicted.
